subject: Clarifying tiered response SLAs, credits cap & on-call retainer
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: maria.gonzalez@acme-analytics.com, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2027-04-03T14:12:00Z
Subject: SLA tiers and on-call coverage questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. My leadership liked Redwood’s latency profile but they pushed back on clarity around guaranteed availability and the economics of premium support. A few specific asks from our side: 

- Can you lay out the uptime tiers you offer, what credit structure applies for missed targets, and whether there’s any cap on credits?
- We need 24/7 escalation coverage for a small set of production endpoints — what does your on-call retainer look like and how do response windows change?
- If we commit to a 12-month reserved pool (dedicated), what discount band can you offer versus on-demand plus the retainer?

We have a procurement call next Friday and I’d like to have a clear pricing + SLA position to present. 

Appreciate any concrete numbers you can provide.

—Jordan
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

P.S. please loop in anyone from your side who owns pricing/legal — procurement will ask about credit caps and force majeure language.

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-04T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA tiers and on-call coverage questions

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artifacts: a one-page SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf and a pricing workbook (Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing.xlsx). High level summary below so you can share with procurement.

SLA / Availability tiers (examples):
- Standard: 99.95% uptime, business-hours (M-F 08:00–18:00 local) P1 response < 4 hours. Credit: 5% of monthly service fee for single-month breach.
- Premium: 99.99% uptime, extended-hours (M-Sun 06:00–22:00) P1 response < 1 hour, 24/7 pager for P0. Credit: 10% of monthly service fee for single-month breach, capped at 30% annually.
- Platinum (enterprise): 99.995% uptime, 24/7 dedicated escalation + named on-call, P1 response < 30 minutes. Credit: 15% monthly, capped at 50% annually; includes a quarterly reliability review.

On-call retainer / escalation options:
- Base support (included): business-hours response SLA as above.
- 24/7 retainer: flat monthly fee (example: $12,000/mo) for a named on-call rotation, guaranteed 1-hour response for P1 and 15-minute pager escalation for P0. Includes up to 8 hours of collaborative war-room time per month; additional hours billed at hourly rate.
- Incident add-on: for priority incidents we can offer a one-time incident response pack (8-hour war-room) at a fixed fee.

Credit and cap notes:
- Credits are calculated on monthly recurring service fees (not variable usage) unless otherwise agreed.
- Standard caps: we typically cap annual aggregated SLA credits at 30% of ARR for Premium, 50% for Platinum; we can negotiate a lower cap if procurement needs a hard ceiling.
- MSS (maintenance & force majeure) windows do not count toward downtime; scheduled windows will be notified 30 days in advance where possible.

Discount / reserved capacity examples (12-month commit):
- 10% discount on platform fees for 1–3 GPU reserved pool equivalent
- 18–22% discount for larger committed capacity tiers (negotiated by volume and committed throughput)
- We can apply an additional 5% loyalty discount for multi-year commitments or prepayment.

Next steps: if you confirm the tier you want (Premium vs Platinum) and an estimated committed GPU-hours / throughput, we’ll return a tailored term sheet with exact numbers and a DocuSign-ready commitment. I’ve proposed sample numbers in the attached workbook.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if procurement wants to walk through the wording.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing.xlsx)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-06T11:47:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA tiers and on-call coverage questions (internal)

Laur — quick internal suggestions before we send anything final to procurement: 

1) Credit methodology: replenish the example with concrete math lines in the workbook — procurement will want to see examples: e.g., if monthly fee = $100k, Premium credit 10% = $10k; if credit cap = 30% ARR we should show a 12-month example.

2) Cap flexibility: offer a lower absolute cap (e.g., 20% of ARR) if they accept a 24-month prepay or a slightly higher reserved commitment. That helps procurement feel protected.

3) Force majeure: procurement often redlines this — propose a mutual language that limits exclusions to events outside reasonable control and requires notice; don’t concede broad carve-outs.

4) On-call retainer pricing: $12k/mo looks fine as a desktop example, but offer a scaled option for smaller customers: $6k/mo for 1-hour response (business-hours to extended-hours), $12k/mo for full 24/7 rotate. That gives procurement room to pick.

5) Add a modest SLA credit floor for repeated breaches (e.g., second consecutive month escalation triggers a 1:1 service credit investigation and a one-time additional 5% remediation credit) — this is a carrot for them and protects Redwood operationally.

I can review the updated workbook and draft a short clause for credits/caps if you want.

—Rishi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme-analytics.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-10T16:45:00Z
Subject: Final proposal: Premium SLA + scaled on-call retainer (proposal attached)

Jordan / Procurement — following our internal review and your ask, attached is an updated one-page summary and a pricing sheet that includes the scaled retainer option. Key points: 

- Recommended: Premium tier (99.99%) + scaled retainer at $6,000/mo (extended-hours 1-hr response) for the first 3 months while we migrate critical endpoints; option to upgrade to $12,000/mo for full 24/7 coverage once traffic ramps.
- SLA credits: Premium = 10% monthly credit; annual cap default 30% of ARR. We’re willing to reduce the cap to 20% of ARR if Acme agrees to a 12-month prepay or a 24-month capacity commit.
- Incident escalation: Named on-call + 8-hour war-room included with the $12k retainer; otherwise incident packs are available per-incident.
- Discounts: 12-month reserved capacity commit => 12% baseline platform discount; sliding scale up to 22% depending on committed volume. Prepay + multi-year locks can add up to 5% additional.

Next steps: I can generate a DocuSign term sheet for the Premium + $6k retainer path so procurement can review with pricing filled in. If you want the reduced credit cap (20% ARR) we’ll need a signed commitment to 12 months prepay or 24 months reserved pool. 

Please let me know which route procurement prefers and I’ll get the formal paperwork started. If helpful, we can also schedule 30–45 minutes to walk legal/procurement through the credit calculation and force majeure language.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
(Attachments: SLA_Tiers_v3.pdf, Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing.xlsx)
